title: Vintage Gibson ES-355 Value Guide: Annual Price Ranges
description: Vintage Gibson ES-355 values from 1958 to 1979, with annual ranges, mono and stereo context, repair considerations and photographs from my guitar archive.
alt: Cherry ES-355 body with two covered humbuckers, four controls and a Bigsby

faqs.q: How Much Is A 1959 Gibson ES-355 Worth?
faqs.a: A clean original cherry 1959 ES-355 has a guide range of $30,000 to $45,000 with factory mono wiring and a Bigsby, or $22,000 to $38,000 with stereo Varitone electronics. These assume excellent condition, original pickups and the original case. Repairs and conversions need a separate appraisal.

A standard-finish 1970 to 1979 stereo ES-355 with its factory vibrato has a guide range of $5,500 to $7,000 in excellent original condition with the original case. I assess repairs and changed parts separately; the range isn't a guaranteed sale price.

faqs.q: Does A Mono Conversion Make A Stereo Guitar Worth The Mono Price?
faqs.a: No. A factory mono guitar and a stereo instrument converted later have different histories. Keeping the removed original harness helps document a conversion, but it doesn't make the guitar factory mono.

faqs.q: Does A Bigsby Automatically Reduce ES-355 Value?
faqs.a: No. A factory vibrato belongs in the standard configuration used by these references. A later installation, removed unit or added holes requires a different comparison. I don't apply the ES-335 stop-tail preference as an automatic ES-355 deduction.

faqs.q: Why Do Several Years Share A Price Range?
faqs.a: Adjacent years can share an era range. The annual rows help you find the year, but the electronics, pickups, condition and original parts still determine the appraisal.

faqs.q: Should I Remove Pickup Covers Before An Appraisal?
faqs.a: No. Start with clear exterior photographs and any existing repair records. Pickup work can damage fragile wiring, and I can explain what further inspection is needed after reviewing the guitar.

faqs.q: Does A Quality Refret Remove All-Original Status?
faqs.a: A quality refret preserves the all-original classification of an otherwise original guitar under this site's grading approach. It takes the guitar out of museum-quality status. Neck reshaping and structural repairs are separate issues.
